title: The Strange Case Of Dr. Jekyll And Mr.

facts: The Project Gutenberg eBook of "The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" was authored by Robert Louis Stevenson.
The eBook was released on June 27, 2008.
The eBook can be accessed online at www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/43.
The text is credited to David Widger.
Mr. Utterson is a reserved and austere lawyer.
Mr. Richard Enfield recounts an incident involving a man named Hyde trampling a young girl.
Enfield and others extorted money from Hyde to avoid scandal.
Hyde possesses a key to a mysterious door.
Mr. Utterson examined Dr. Jekyll's will after dinner.
Dr. Jekyll's will bequeathed all his possessions to Edward Hyde.
Dr. Lanyon had not seen Jekyll in over a decade.
Utterson discovered that Hyde had a key to Jekyll's laboratory.
Dr. Jekyll hosted a dinner for a few close friends, including Mr. Utterson.
Utterson expressed concerns about Jekyll's connection to Mr. Hyde.
Jekyll urged Utterson to promise to look after Hyde's interests after his departure.
Utterson agreed to Jekyll's request to ensure justice for Hyde.
Sir Danvers Carew was murdered by Mr. Hyde in October of 18—.
A maid witnessed the altercation between Carew and Hyde from her window.
Mr. Utterson identified the broken cane at the crime scene as one he had given to Dr. Henry Jekyll.
Hyde's living quarters were found to be luxurious yet ransacked, indicating his hasty departure.
Mr. Utterson visits Dr. Jekyll in the late afternoon.
Dr. Jekyll expresses concern for his reputation after the murder of Sir Danvers Carew.
Jekyll shows Utterson a letter from Edward Hyde.
Mr. Guest notes the similar handwriting between Jekyll's letter and Hyde's letter.
Mr. Hyde vanished after the murder of Sir Danvers.
Dr. Jekyll became increasingly reclusive after a brief period of social engagement.
Dr. Lanyon was gravely ill and refused to discuss Jekyll.
Lanyon left Utterson a sealed letter to be opened only after Jekyll's death or disappearance.
Mr. Utterson and Mr. Enfield stop in front of the door associated with Mr. Hyde.
Utterson expresses concern for Dr. Jekyll during their walk.
Dr. Jekyll appears very low and reluctant to join Utterson and Enfield outside.
Jekyll suddenly displays a look of terror while conversing with Utterson and Enfield.
Mr. Utterson is visited by Poole, Dr. Jekyll's butler.
Utterson and Poole find a lifeless body believed to be Hyde in Jekyll's cabinet.
A will is found that names Utterson as the beneficiary.
Utterson decides to examine the documents before involving the police.
Dr. Lanyon received a registered letter from Dr. Henry Jekyll on January 9th.
Jekyll instructed Lanyon to retrieve a specific drawer from his cabinet.
At midnight, a mysterious man arrived to collect the drawer's contents.
The man consumed a potion and transformed into Jekyll before Lanyon's eyes.
Dr. Henry Jekyll created a potion that transformed him into Edward Hyde.
Jekyll became horrified by Hyde's violent actions, including murder.
Jekyll's attempts to renounce Hyde ultimately failed.
